items.narrative:
The audit covers 48 supply-chain events recorded between 2025-02-05 and 2025-06-15, spanning 14 products and 6 external trading partners. Of those 14 products, 5 are definitively on the Food Traceability List, 6 are classified as suspicious (meaning they may also fall under traceability requirements), and only 3 are confirmed off-list. Event types range across cooling (3), first land-based receiving (3), harvesting (6), initial packing (6), receiving (6), transformation (5), and shipping (19), giving a broad but uneven footprint across critical tracking events.

The most serious gaps are the 8 high-severity findings, followed by 33 medium-severity findings, totalling 41 findings across the audit. The single largest finding category is scope or exemption uncertainty, which accounts for 8 findings and directly reflects the 6 suspicious products whose traceability obligations remain unresolved. Four ftl_declared_mismatch findings show that products 10860004520020, 10860004520037, 10860004520099, and 10860004520113 are all declared as 'General grocery' yet are flagged as suspicious or definitively on the traceability list, meaning their declared category is almost certainly wrong. Five inbound ERP mismatches indicate that incoming shipment records do not reconcile with internal data, and 21 key data elements are missing out of 450 graded, yielding a KDE coverage rate of 0.9533. Lot integrity is also fragile: 2 backward-lineage gaps, 2 date-ordering anomalies, 2 duplicate TLC flags, and a self-receive anomaly collectively undermine the chain of custody narrative.

Immediately prioritise reclassifying products 10860004520020, 10860004520037, 10860004520099, and 10860004520113 with a qualified regulatory reviewer to resolve the 8 scope or exemption uncertainty findings before any other remediation work. Then address Metro Grocers Inc and Sunbelt Restaurants Group directly: both carry a band-D data-quality rating, accounting for 11 and 8 events respectively, and their records are the primary source of the 5 inbound ERP mismatches and 2 partner data-quality findings. Closing the 21 missing KDEs and resolving the 2 backward-lineage gaps should follow as a parallel workstream, since those deficiencies will surface immediately in any regulatory traceback exercise.
